question:
We are planning a project that depends on a third-party API nobody on the team has used and on a performance target we may not be able to reach. How should we handle these things that could go wrong, both when planning the work and while it is under way?

Answer with a list of guidelines. After each guideline, cite the source it comes from: the path of the SWEBOK file if you have it, otherwise a verbatim quote of at least 8 words from the passage, in the form (source: ...).
answer:
# Summary

When facing unknown third-party APIs and uncertain performance targets, teams should identify and register risks early, analyze probability and impact, build prototypes to explore unknowns, monitor risks continuously throughout the project, and be prepared to adapt plans, apply corrective actions, or recalculate risk exposure as new information emerges.

# Guidelines

- Identify risk factors, analyze their probability and potential impact, prioritize them, and develop mitigation strategies to reduce the probability of negative events and minimize [SWEBOK excerpt 1400cd0d41734de0e233]; capture this in a risk register. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Risk Management and Quality Assessment/Risk Management_ Identification, Analysis, and Mitigation Strategies.md)

- Use risk assessment methods such as [SWEBOK excerpt bb228fe333a5104c91f2] to identify and evaluate risk factors, including risks related to software quality requirements. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Risk Management and Quality Assessment/Risk Assessment Methods and Software Project Risk Management.md)

- Perform risk management [SWEBOK excerpt 3f32cf09481746d60739]. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Risk Management and Quality Assessment/Continuous Risk and Quality Management/Risk Management Throughout Project Life Cycle.md)

- Use prototyping to explore the least-understood software aspects or components first, since this approach contrasts with methods that begin with the best-understood portions and can surface unknowns about a third-party API or performance feasibility early. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Engineering Processes and Quality Assurance/Formal Methods, Agile Development, and Software Quality/Verification and Prototyping Approaches/Prototyping Methods in Software Engineering.md)

- Use simulation and prototyping as [SWEBOK excerpt 77f6472e3b0024f4f550], to predict behavior and validate performance instead of relying entirely on testing. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Design Quality Evaluation and Assessment/Design Analysis and Quality Metrics/Formal Analysis and Dynamic Evaluation Techniques.md)

- Use risk management tools such as [SWEBOK excerpt a4094c54e1db764ace17] [SWEBOK excerpt 07c3add5f73a901c739d]. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Engineering Processes and Quality Assurance/Software Engineering Processes, Lifecycles, and Measurement/Data Collection, Quality Assurance, and Project Monitoring/Project Tracking and Risk Management Tools.md)

- Adopt a risk-driven approach to architecture: do just enough software architecture to mitigate identified risks, particularly where risks could result from extremely demanding quality requirements or possible high-risk failures. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Foundations of Software Architecture/Software Architecture Foundations and Design Principles/Software Architecture_ Foundations, Methods, and Modern Practice/Risk-Driven Software Architecture Approach.md)

- Analyze scaling, performance properties, and resource consumption properties as key architectural concerns during design, addressing them as part of iterative analysis, synthesis, and evaluation. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Foundations of Software Architecture/Software Architecture Foundations and Design Principles/Software Architecture_ Contexts, Methods, and Design Processes/Architecture Analysis and Synthesis/Architectural Design Analysis and Key Concerns.md)

- Ensure requirements are feasible—meaning [SWEBOK excerpt 1f1c1333967b74fab0f5]—and that performance requirements are testable, i.e., compliance or noncompliance can be clearly demonstrated. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Requirements_ Foundations and Engineering Practices/Requirements Engineering_ Elicitation, Analysis, and Specification/Requirements Analysis and Refinement/Software Requirements Properties and Quality Criteria.md)

- Continually monitor adherence to scope, project plan, and related plans; revisit the project risk profile; and evaluate adherence to software quality requirements at predetermined intervals. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Quality Management and Project Oversight/Software Acquisition and Project Oversight/Data Acquisition and Project Measurement/Implementation and Monitoring of Software Project Measurement.md)

- Recalculate risk exposures regularly and report outcomes when thresholds have been exceeded, enabling problem detection and exception identification. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Quality Management and Project Oversight/Software Acquisition and Project Oversight/Risk Monitoring and Control Management/Risk Exposure Recalculation and Threshold Monitoring.md)

- When project monitoring reveals issues, make changes such as corrective actions (e.g., retesting certain software components), and where appropriate revise the project plan to accommodate unanticipated events; document and communicate all decisions to relevant parties. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Quality Management and Project Oversight/Software Acquisition and Project Oversight/Risk Monitoring and Control Management/Software Project Control and Configuration Management.md)

- When acquiring third-party software components, verify [SWEBOK excerpt b3a7cf59bc0d0a7639a0] with architectural design and requirements; integrate the components; and validate [SWEBOK excerpt 187243ef7157884fdd70] in their intended operating environment. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Quality Management and Project Oversight/Software Acquisition and Project Oversight/Software Acquisition and Supplier Contract Management.md)

- Assess the technical risk of implementation as one of the factors relevant to prioritizing requirements, so that high-risk items such as the unknown API integration or the demanding performance target receive appropriate attention. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Requirements Validation and Management/Requirements Management and Prioritization Strategy/Requirement Prioritization Schemes and Factors.md)

- Conduct system functional or preliminary design reviews to ensure the system can proceed into further design with acceptable risk and that all functional and performance requirements are defined and consistent with budget, schedule, risk, and other constraints. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Engineering Processes and Quality Assurance/Software Quality Assurance and Verification Standards/Quality Assurance Reviews and Implementation Practices/Technical Reviews and Audits in Project Management.md)

- Incorporate [SWEBOK excerpt dfb53af98c247d088046] to help improve product quality, as risk management can [SWEBOK excerpt f567f49e96e9f6c2dd4e]. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Engineering Processes and Quality Assurance/Software Quality Assurance and Verification Standards/Software Quality Management and Process Improvement/Software Quality Management and Organizational Support/Management Support and Software Quality Processes.md)

- Conduct a project retrospective analysis [SWEBOK excerpt 1fcd2e4b5300383cd5ac], and feed lessons learned into organizational learning and improvement endeavors. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Quality Management and Project Oversight/Software Measurement and Organizational Learning/Software Engineering Measurement and Organizational Learning.md)
